title: Books
text:
Statistics, data science and artificial intelligence for the social sciences.
My books bridge mathematical foundations, statistical methodology and computational practice. They are designed for students, researchers and practitioners interested in developing rigorous, reproducible approaches to quantitative social science, from introductory statistics to modern artificial intelligence.

title: Diego Andrés Pérez Ruiz
text:
Lecturer in Social Statistics · Researcher



I develop statistical methods for learning from complex and imperfect data — combining Bayesian inference, survey methodology and artificial intelligence to advance quantitative social science.


About me Research Download CV


GitHub · Scholar · ORCID · University profile · Email





  Illustration: three overlapping probability density curves
Currently
I am a Lecturer in Social Statistics at the University of Manchester, where my research focuses on Bayesian statistical methodology, survey inference, data integration and computational statistics.
My current work explores how probability and non-probability data sources can be combined to improve statistical inference, how information theory can guide data collection and integration, and how artificial intelligence can support rigorous and reproducible social science research.
Alongside my research, I teach postgraduate courses in statistics, machine learning and advanced quantitative methods, develop open-source computational resources, and write about data science and artificial intelligence.
Focus areas

title: Diego Andrés Pérez Ruiz
text:
Research Interests


Bayesian Statistics
Bayesian modelling, hierarchical models, posterior inference and uncertainty quantification.


Survey Data Integration
Integration of probability and non-probability samples, selection bias and population-level inference.


Information Theory and Adaptive Survey Design
Entropy-based stopping rules, estimand-aware prioritisation and information-driven data collection.


Artificial Intelligence and Computational Social Science
AI-augmented data, statistical validity, machine learning and reproducible computational methodology.

title: About
text:
Diego Perez Ruiz
AI Specialist & Statistician

  
  
  




Thanks for stopping by. I’m an AI specialist and statistician based in Manchester, working at the meeting point of statistics and artificial intelligence.
My work centres on AI and machine learning, functional data and nonparametric statistics — methods for making sense of large, noisy datasets and separating the consistent patterns from the noise. I currently work as a Data Analyst at Mosscare St Vincent’s Housing Group, and previously held research posts in statistics at the University of Manchester.
You can see what I’ve been building on the Projects and Software pages, or get in touch here.
Biography
I am broadly interested in statistical theory and methodology, with a particular focus on functional data and nonparametric statistics. Statistics matters more than ever because of the ease with which we now collect large amounts of data — and the real challenge is sorting through it to separate consistent patterns from noise. How best to use the tools that let us do that is the focus of my work.
I completed my PhD in Mathematical Sciences at the University of Manchester. Before Manchester, I did an MSc in Statistics and Probability at the Center for Mathematical Research (CIMAT), and prior to that a BSc in Applied Mathematics and Computer Science at the National Autonomous University of Mexico (UNAM).

title: Hello from a Quarto site
text:
Welcome to the new site. It’s built with Quarto, which means posts like this one can mix prose with live R, Python, or Julia — the same tools I use day to day.
Here’s a code block to prove the point (display-only for now):
library(ggplot2)

# kernel density estimate — the motif in the site logo
ggplot(faithful, aes(waiting)) +
  geom_density(fill = "#1E5C4A", alpha = 0.15, colour = "#1E5C4A") +
  theme_minimal()
To make code actually execute when the site builds, install R (or Python/Julia) and set execute: true in the front matter. More soon.

title: Predicting hypoglycaemia from CGM in CHI
text: Modelling the prediction of hypoglycaemia from continuous glucose monitoring (CGM) in congenital hyperinsulinism (CHI). title: Probabilistic modelling of cycling-accident risk
text: Cycling is an often-overlooked mode of transport for both commuting and recreation, and one that has grown in popularity — while being environmentally friendly, economical, and healthy. This project builds probabilistic models of cycling-accident risk, using Greater Manchester as a case study.
